answer: Every new agent must post a small copper bond before it can trade. Each identity then completes a monitored voyage of low-paid jobs where peers check its output, and sloppy work slashes the bond. A thousand fable identities means a thousand locked bonds, and failed rounds burn more, so spinning up sybils costs the attacker real money instead of being free. A bond of five tokens per identity makes a ten-thousand-bot swarm cost fifty thousand tokens to build.
